title: EffectiveCommunicationOutput
description: Structured communication coaching output: effectiveness scores, priority improvements with rewrites, missed opportunities, filler/hedging patterns, talk-time signal, next-meeting gameplan, and evidence citations — all grounded in transcript evidence.

executive_summary.description: 2-4 sentence overview of communication effectiveness: overall impression, key strengths, and the most impactful area for improvement.

overall_effectiveness_score.description: Composite communication effectiveness score. 0 = ineffective, 100 = exceptional.

communication_status.description: Categorical assessment of overall communication quality.

coach_take.description: Candid, direct coaching perspective — what a trusted advisor would say privately. Actionable and specific.

score_breakdown.description: Granular scores across seven communication dimensions.

what_worked.description: Specific things the speaker did well. Each entry is a concrete, evidence-grounded observation.

priority_improvements.description: Top communication improvements ranked by impact. Each includes diagnosis, evidence, a before/after rewrite, and a practice drill.

missed_opportunities.description: Moments in the conversation where a different approach would have been more effective.

filler_or_hedging_patterns.description: Recurring filler words, hedge phrases, or verbal tics that undermine authority or clarity.

talk_time_signal.description: Assessment of the user's share of speaking time and whether it was appropriate for their role.

next_meeting_gameplan.description: Concrete preparation plan for the next similar meeting.

one_thing_to_change_next_meeting.description: The single highest-leverage behavior change to implement immediately.

citations.description: Verbatim transcript quotes supporting the analysis. At least three required.

metadata.description: Analysis metadata: which input mode and analysis depth were used, and when the output was generated.

clarity.description: How clear and unambiguous the communication was.

brevity.description: Economy of words — saying what needs to be said without excess.

structure.description: Logical organization of points, use of framing and signposting.

audience_alignment.description: How well the communication was calibrated to the audience's needs, seniority, and context.

executive_presence.description: Confidence, authority, and gravitas in delivery.

action_orientation.description: Driving toward decisions, next steps, and clear ownership.

listening_and_responsiveness.description: Acknowledging others' points, building on input, adapting in real time.

theme.description: Short label for the improvement area. Example: 'Hedging undermines recommendations'.

diagnosis.description: What the speaker is doing and why it's a problem.

why_it_costs_you.description: Concrete impact on credibility, outcomes, or perception.

impact_level.description: How much fixing this would improve overall effectiveness.

evidence.description: Verbatim transcript evidence demonstrating the pattern.

rewrite.description: Before/after example showing how to improve.

drill.description: A specific practice exercise to build the new habit.

approximate_location.description: Where in the transcript this appears. Examples: 'opening remarks', 'during budget discussion', 'closing'.

before.description: The original statement or paraphrase from the transcript.

after.description: Improved version demonstrating the coaching point.

why_better.description: Explanation of what changed and why it's more effective.

moment.description: When in the conversation the opportunity occurred.

what_happened.description: What the speaker actually did or said.

better_move.description: What they should have done instead and why.

sample_line.description: Example script the speaker could have used.

pattern.description: The filler word, hedge phrase, or verbal tic. Example: 'I think maybe we should...', 'sort of', 'basically'.

count_estimate.description: Approximate frequency in the transcript. Example: '4-5 times', 'throughout'.

replacement_pattern.description: What to say instead. Example: 'We should...' (drop the hedge).

user_share_estimate.description: Estimated percentage of total talk time. Example: '~35%', '~60%'.

balance_assessment.description: Whether the user's share was appropriate for their role and goal.

note.description: Context on why the balance is appropriate or problematic.

opening_script.description: Suggested opening statement for the next similar meeting.

three_non_negotiables.description: Three communication behaviors to commit to in the next meeting. Exactly three required.

pushback_response_template.description: A template for handling pushback or disagreement gracefully.

closing_script.description: Suggested closing statement to end the meeting with clarity and ownership.

change.description: The single behavior change to implement.

why.description: Why this specific change will have the most impact.

success_signal.description: How the user will know they've successfully made the change.

approximate_location.description: Where in the transcript this appears.

mode_used.description: Which input mode was detected. 'transcript_only' if no optional context fields were provided; 'transcript_plus_context' otherwise.

analysis_depth_used.description: Which analysis depth was applied. Mirrors the input analysis_depth field; defaults to 'standard' if not specified.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this analysis was generated.
